newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei futures end off as upside moves fail.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei futures end off as upside moves fail.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures ended scarcely changed as players squared their positions after efforts to test the upside failed ahead of the weekend.

News that Nissan Mutual Life Insurance Co had been ordered to halt operations by Japan's Finance Ministry had a muted impact as the market had already absorbed the news during overnight Chicago trade, dealers said.
The benchmark Nikkei 225 June contract ended five points easier at 18,650 after testing a high of 18,840. The downside remained supported at 18,520.
"A lot of people think this could be an isolated problem. That's why the market didn't go lower," a trader with a Japanese futures house said.
"But it couldn't break 18,850 after repeated attempts. So people who were holding long positions decided to get out before the weekend," he added.
He said the June Nikkei remained on track for its target of 19,000 points, while any dips towards 18,500 would represent good buying opportunities.

The April MSCI Taiwan index contract ended at 359.8 against its opening 357.0 on volume of 1,491 lots. May was at 355.7 against 354.5 on 655 lots as players rolled over their positions ahead of April's expiry on Tuesday.
Refco (Singapore) Pte Ltd said in a daily commentary the April contract's drop to a 5.5 discount to the cash index during the day provided a good buying opportunity.
But it said the Taipei stock market would be looking for more good news on corporate earnings and economic figures before attempting the 8,700 level on its cash index.
